adjudication_summary: Source-reviewed rework closed the prior framework-test blocker by replacing scaffold-level database/activity/mechanism conclusions with paper-local evidence. Ramosin is supported as a C-terminally amidated 16-aa peptide with in vitro antibacterial activity and low hemolysis/cytotoxicity under tested conditions; source conflicts are preserved for database rows whose exact numeric values are not tabulated locally.

per_layer_decision_rationale.layer_1_database: Ramosin identity, literature linkage, and five core antibacterial thresholds are source-supported; terminal amidation normalization and several exact database-only percentages remain explicit cautions/source_conflicts rather than being promoted to source_verified.
per_layer_decision_rationale.layer_2_activity_toxicity: Final records use primary source text and figure/supplement captions. The prior Table 1 APD3 property misparse is not promoted into final activity evidence.
per_layer_decision_rationale.layer_3_mechanism: SEM supports S. aureus membrane disturbance directly; E. coli SEM is negative under the tested condition; structural and LPS/teichoic-acid content is bounded as support or hypothesis.
per_layer_decision_rationale.publication_grade_decision: Accepted with cautions because all owner-layer blockers are resolved, source conflicts are explicit, no rework target remains open, and unsupported exact values were not fabricated.

caution_findings.evidence_context: APD6/DBAASP sequence snapshots store the Ramosin backbone while Tables 2 and 4 report the synthesized peptide with C-terminal amidation.
DBAASP exact cytotoxicity/hemolysis and screening percentage rows are not tabulated as exact values in local source text; qualitative source support is preserved but rows remain source_conflict.
Packet analysis activity scaffold misread Table 1 APD3 property rows as IC50 activity rows; final activity rows are source-reviewed and do not promote those scaffold rows.
Direct mechanism evidence is limited to SEM membrane disturbance in S. aureus; E. coli SEM is negative under the tested condition and LPS/teichoic-acid statements are discussion-level hypotheses.
